clue.text: Battle where protagonists bolster each other?

definitions.text: Battle where protagonists bolster each other?

parts.words: Battle where protagonists bolster each other?
parts.note: bolster usually means to support, but a bolster is also a long pillow, so the fighters are whacking one another with bedding

explanation.surface: A contest in which the rivals oddly prop each other up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolster' reads as a verb meaning support; here it is the long bedroom cushion used as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful bedroom scuffle in which children swing cushions at each other is exactly the battle described.

clue.text: Plans I had when touring the east

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the other letters wrap around this one

parts.note: I had contracts to I'D
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone's plans were made while they were travelling in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' standing for AS is a common crossword equivalence, as in 'as I left'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans and notions are both thoughts about what to do, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Could sir initially undertake manoeuvres? That's daft!

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests moving things about, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word undertake

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a knight being able to carry out military exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' shuffles COULDSIR plus U (the first letter of 'undertake'); 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd or ridiculous is daft, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Girl, briefly, is going to mother

indicators.note: briefly asks for a word cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: will expresses the future, as is going to does
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A young woman is briefly said to be heading off to visit her mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the last L from WILL, leaving WIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilma is a female first name, as in Wilma Flintstone, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Local resident of Tampere, maybe, loudly dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so this letter is removed from the word

parts.note: Tampere is a city in Finland, so someone living there is a Finn
f (forte) is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A Finnish neighbour from Tampere is noisily sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's nearby pub. 'dismissed' removes F from FINN.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a local is the neighbourhood pub, and a pub is a kind of tavern serving drinks.

clue.text: Husband to display code number that's used for locks

parts.note: to air something is to show it publicly
a PIN is a personal identification number, a numeric code

explanation.surface: A husband shows off a secret number used for opening locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests doors and combination codes, but it means locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent pin holds locks of hair in place, so it is an item used for tresses.

clue.text: I agree to attend old comedy show

parts.note: yes is how one says I agree
to minister to someone is to attend to their needs

explanation.surface: Someone accepts an invitation to go to a classic sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes Minister was a 1980s BBC sitcom about a government minister and his civil servants.
explanation.definitionFit: This British political sitcom from the 1980s is an instance of a vintage television comedy.

clue.text: I can heed PLP after reshuffling old cabinet?

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges a cabinet, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A prime minister vows to listen to Labour MPs after a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: PLP is the Parliamentary Labour Party; 'cabinet' means a piece of furniture, not ministers, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chippendale's eighteenth-century furniture style names antique cupboards and chairs, so an old cabinet may be one.

clue.text: Correct me when returning before the finish

indicators.note: before places the reversed word ahead of the next piece
returning means going back, so the word me is read backwards

parts.note: the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be put right when they come back before the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend or revise a text is to correct it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Taking part in decathlon, GIs habitually rather stretched

indicators.note: Taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: American soldiers competing in a decathlon are usually rather extended.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat long or fairly lengthy is what rather stretched means.

clue.text: Chum is all you need to make this entertainment

indicators.note: to make here means to form something new out of these letters by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A friend is all one needs for a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges CHUMISALL; 'you need' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety theatre with songs and comic turns was a popular form of entertainment in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Someone who dwells above bank in the city

indicators.note: in a down answer, above puts the first piece on top of the next

parts.note: a liver is one who lives, i.e. dwells, somewhere
a pool is a common fund or bank of resources

explanation.surface: A city resident lives in a flat above a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a major port city in north-west England, an example of a city.

clue.text: Freelance photographer very quietly penning article

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen for animals, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: pp (pianissimo) is the musical direction for very quiet
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A freelance photographer silently writes a piece for a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' suggests writing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pap is short for paparazzo, the freelance snapper chasing celebrities.

clue.text: Lunatic getting post with teaching union

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A madman lands a position along with membership of a teachers' union.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was the UK's National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy person is informally called a nutcase, and this slang word is a synonym for lunatic.

clue.text: Film of Kojak, maybe, with people

parts.note: Kojak, the TV detective played by Telly Savalas, had the first name Theo
men are people

explanation.surface: A movie starring the bald TV detective with a cast of others.
explanation.walkthrough: Kojak was a 1970s US police drama; the lieutenant's first name was Theo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Omen is a 1976 horror movie about the Antichrist, an example of a film.

clue.text: A meeting place in wide street

parts.note: a venue is a place where people meet

explanation.surface: A spot to gather on a broad thoroughfare.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad road, often tree-lined, in a town is called a boulevard or similar, matching wide street.

clue.text: Get a letter read out

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so we want the word that sounds like this letter

parts.note: the letter C is one letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone receives a letter and has it read aloud to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a joke is to understand it, and that sense of grasping is what the verb means.

clue.text: A sign in desert perhaps showing name of Central Asian city

indicators.note: in says the letters for a sign go inside the desert word

parts.note: sand is what a desert typically consists of
a mark is a sign

explanation.surface: A signpost in the desert points the way to an ancient Silk Road city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing name of' is a link; Samarkand is in today's Uzbekistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Samarkand is an ancient Silk Road city in Uzbekistan, in Central Asia.

clue.text: Gets together some charcuterie for picking up?

indicators.note: picking up means catching by ear, so the answer sounds like the cured cuts

parts.note: charcuterie is cured cold cuts, i.e. meats

explanation.surface: A gathering where someone collects a selection of cured cold cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' suggests collecting food; it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: When people assemble or come together, they convene, so the verb phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Man, say, following a passage

indicators.note: following puts the island word after the single letter

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A man walks behind someone along a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; it is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats or shelves is a gangway, matching passage.

clue.text: Seamen not normally crossing south, as a whole

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the rearranged letters go around this one
not normally means arranged in an unusual way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Sailors behaving unusually all cross to the south together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not normally' gives ENMASE from SEAMEN, and 'crossing' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means all together, everyone at once, so it is a synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Wrong function

definitions.meaning: a wrong is a misdeed or transgression
the abbreviation for sine, a trigonometric function

explanation.definitionFit: A transgression is a wrong, and sin is the shortened name of the sine trigonometric function.

clue.text: Diver to employ in round pool, ultimately

parts.note: O is round in shape
to use something is to employ it

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of the word pool

explanation.surface: A diver is hired to work in a circular swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The water ousel, or dipper, is a bird that dives into streams; 'Diver' looks like a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The water ousel, also called the dipper, is a bird that plunges under streams for food, so it is a diving bird.

clue.text: Lennie's pose affected while resting?

indicators.note: affected means altered, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Lennie strikes an unnatural pose while lying down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' looks like it describes the pose as fake, but it shuffles LENNIESPOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying peacefully at night is described by this phrase, so while resting is a gentle, slightly whimsical gloss.
